craft.heading: Heading
wx.title: Weather
freq.search: an airport code, a frequency, or a position
atis.hint: Tune a field with an ATIS and its wording appears here.
set.ui_language_why: What this window is written in. It does not change what is spoken on the radio, which follows the aeroplane.
set.radio_effects_why: The band-limited AM channel, not the raw voice
set.operator_why: A controller is somebody in a room, not a file being played. They take a moment after keying up, they are never quite the same loudness twice, and once in a while they say “uh”.
set.breathing_why: An audible breath in the gaps of a long clearance
set.wind_why: Wind gusting under the voice, the way an open tower cab sounds
set.hesitation_why: The occasional “uh” before the callsign. Rare on purpose.
set.button_why: Press the one you want to talk on. Nobody publishes which number a yoke calls its buttons.
set.ptt_why: Use one the simulator does not need. The panel's own button works either way.
set.no_controller: no controller found — pip install pygame-ce
set.no_controller_found: no controller connected — plug one in and reopen this screen
set.controller_offline: Known to this computer but not connected: {names}
set.spoken_language_why: Follows the aeroplane. English everywhere, plus the local language over a state that works one. Speak either; the controller answers in the one you used.
set.handoffs_why: Name the next frequency when you outfly this one
set.simbrief_why: Fill the flight in from your latest plan instead of typing it twice.
set.simbrief_no_user: Put your SimBrief username in Settings first.
set.ground_why: No taxi clearance while the tug or the jetway is still attached
set.ground_call_why: An approved pushback calls one, through GSX’s own menu
set.ground_voice_why: “Ground crew, request pushback” — and boarding, fuel, catering or de-icing
set.traffic_why: Airlines that belong at this field, each crew in its own language
set.traffic_callsigns_why: Airline callsigns are what a large field really carries; registrations are easier to follow, because you hear the letters rather than a name you have to know.
set.real_obs_why: METARs from the NOAA Aviation Weather Center
set.sim_wins_why: Custom weather in the sim has to match the ATIS
set.sim_stand_in: no simulator — flying on a stand-in position
set.rules_plus: Understanding: rules, with {model} for anything they miss.
set.saved_restart: saved — restart WilcoATC for this to take effect
log.traffic_visible: Traffic will be visible in the simulator.
log.traffic_observed: Working {count} aircraft from the simulator's own traffic.
log.traffic_spawned_holding: {callsign} is holding short of runway {runway} until the runway is free.
log.traffic_spawn_failed: The simulator could not create {callsign}, so it is not on the runway.
log.placed: No simulator, so placing the aircraft at {airport}.
log.bilingual: {where}: {language} is worked here alongside English. Speak either; the controller answers in the one you used.
log.ptt: Push to talk: hold the {key_name} key.
log.ptt_button: Push to talk: hold joystick {stick} button {button}.
log.tuned_advisory: {mhz} — {station}: an advisory frequency, so nobody answers. Announce your position and listen out.
log.human_online: {mhz} — {station} is working this frequency on {network}. WilcoATC will stay quiet on it.
log.empty_frequency: {mhz} — nobody is listening on this frequency here.{hint}
log.still_working: Still working on the last transmission.
log.nobody_listening: No station is listening on this frequency.
log.transmit_stuck: The transmit button has been down for {seconds} seconds, so the transmission was ended. Nothing else could be said while it was.
log.cabin_no_audio: The cabin and the first officer cannot reach the speaker. The radio is unaffected. ({detail})
log.crew_no_voice: The crew cannot be synthesised, so the cabin is silent. The radio is unaffected. ({detail})
log.announcements_missing: No announcements folder called "{folder}". The cabin is using its own voices.
log.announcements_empty: Recorded announcements are switched on, but no audio files were found. The cabin is using its own voices.
log.unpublished: {mhz} is not in the published data for {airport}. Answering as {station}. To keep it: wilcoatc freq {airport} --add {position} {mhz}
notice.title: This is alpha software
notice.body: WilcoATC is in alpha. You will run into bugs, and you will run into a lot of them.
notice.point1: The controller can say the wrong thing, or something that makes no sense at all.
notice.point2: It can fail to understand you, or hear something you never said.
notice.point3: Anything here can change or stop working from one version to the next.
notice.agree: I know what I am getting into, and I am using this at my own risk.
flight.title: Flight
flight.why: The simulator supplies your position and radios. These are the details it cannot tell us.
order.heading: heading
log.departure_moved: The aircraft is at {airport}, not {was}. Using {airport}.
log.sim_lost: Lost the simulator. Looking for it again.
log.sim_waiting: Simulator not detected. Waiting for it, and flying from the manually set aircraft state until it appears.
log.type_moved: The simulator has a {type}, not a {was}.
map.follow_title: Keep the map on the aircraft
map.no_controller: no controller within range of you
set.immersion_why: The rest of the aeroplane. A first officer in the other seat and a cabin crew behind you, following the flight the same way the controller does. None of it goes out on the radio, and none of it changes what ATC says.
set.copilot_why: Callouts, checklists and the numbers read back to you
set.callouts_why: Eighty knots, V one, rotate, positive rate, and the calls on the way down
set.confirmations_why: Says the numbers back to you on the interphone, so two of you heard them
set.checklists_why: Called and answered at the points a flight actually runs them
set.readbacks_why: Reads a clearance back if you have not, after a few seconds. Off unless you want it: the point of the radio is usually to work it yourself.
set.cabin_crew_why: A purser and a cabin, on the address system
set.briefings_why: The demonstration during the taxi out, and the crew calls around it
set.announcements_why: Welcome aboard, the cruise, the descent, and where you have arrived
set.service_why: The trolley after the climb, and a call to the flight deck before it
set.chimes_why: The two notes before an announcement, and the seatbelt sign
set.boarding_music_why: Plays quietly in the cabin while people get on, and stops at pushback
set.crew_manner: Who they are, and how much
set.airline_name: What the crew call the airline
set.airline_why: Left empty, they take it from your callsign, and say “this flight” for a private registration.
set.captain_name_why: Left empty, one is cast from the registration, and the same aeroplane keeps the same captain.
set.talk_to_crew_why: Say “cabin crew” or “ground crew” first, and they answer instead of the controller
set.use_sim: Take the aircraft from the simulator
set.use_sim_why: Off, the aeroplane sits where you put it and nothing moves
log.traffic_refused: This simulator will not create AI aircraft, so WilcoATC adds no traffic of its own. Aircraft already in the simulator are still worked.
set.use_recordings_why: A real announcement beats a synthesised one. Where a recording exists for a moment, it is played instead.
set.announcements_dir_why: Leave it empty to use the folder beside WilcoATC, or point it at a pack you already have. The layout is the one the Fenix A320 uses, so a pack made for that aeroplane works in any of them.
set.components_why: The voices, the nav database and the speech recogniser are too big to ship with the program, so they are downloaded once. About 1.5 GB in total.
set.data_credits: Enroute sectors: VatGlasses contributors, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
setup.title: Getting the pieces
setup.why: Three things are too big to ship inside the program and are downloaded once: the voices your controllers speak with, the database of every airport and frequency, and the model that hears you. About 1.5 GB, and you only do this once.
setup.retry: Something did not download. Check the connection and try again: what already arrived is kept.
setup.leave_open: You can close this and carry on. The download keeps going.
setup.extra_voices_why: 400 MB more. Gives the German, Dutch and French positions a real voice instead of the older synthesiser.
setup.restart: Downloaded. Restart WilcoATC to use it.
doctor.title: Diagnostics
doctor.why: The same check wilcoatc doctor runs in a terminal: every part of the program, whether it is there, and what it found.
log.voices_missing: The controller voices have not been downloaded yet. Open Settings, then Components, and press Download.
log.hq_missing: The cloned voices are not installed, so the controllers are using the standard voices. Download the cloning model with: {command}
alert.no_voices: The controllers have no voice yet
setup.ready: Downloaded. The controllers have their voices.
log.no_enroute_frequency: No enroute frequency is published for this area ({sector}). Staying with the radar controller you are on. Add one with: {command} <ICAO> --add CTR <frequency> --name <name>
set.applause_why: The cabin claps when you touch down gentler than 200 feet per minute
set.landing_report_why: A few seconds after touchdown: the landing rate, how smooth it was, and the flight against its SimBrief schedule
landing.title: Landing report
landing.no_plan: Load a SimBrief plan to compare this flight against its schedule.
set.crew_realism_why: A little interphone and cabin speaker on their voices, and the odd um and er
set.bilingual_why: A crew whose language is not English repeat each cabin announcement in English
